Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:1: After the previous chapters have explained the nature of the blemish itself, let us now proceed to explain how many kinds of blemish a person causes, so that he may fear to sin upon seeing how much evil he causes to himself, to his soul, and to all the worlds.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:2: The first is a blemish in his own body, which is made in the stamped image of the pattern of the supernal worlds; and when one of his limbs is blemished, he is a person with a defect, and the Shechinah does not rest upon him. This is explained in the Tikkunim (130b), in these words: "and in every single limb, which is a candle for every commandment, a person must crown the Holy One, blessed be He, and prepare for it a clean, pure place to rest there; and therefore a person must clear away from every single limb all thoughts and evil, filthy ponderings, which are the husks [kelipot], and must illuminate them with all the commandments that rest upon every limb through those candles - for every commandment is called a candle, as it is said (Proverbs 6:23), 'for the commandment is a candle' - 'the candle of the LORD is the soul of man' (ibid. 20:27) - and with it one must search all the innermost chambers, and clear away from them leaven and chametz, chaff and straw," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:3: And it says further on: "but the Holy One, blessed be He - His dominion is in every place, like the soul, whose dominion is over every single limb; 'the whole earth is full of His glory' - in every place a person calls to Him, He answers him; except that in the place of that limb which is blemished through the sin a person commits, the Holy One, blessed be He, does not rest in that limb, of which it is said (Leviticus 21:18), 'any man who has a defect shall not draw near.'"
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:4: And a person's limbs are all arranged according to the order of creation, and therefore a person is called a "small world" [microcosm]; and whoever crowns the Holy One, blessed be He, over every single limb is as though he crowned Him over the entire world" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:5: And it says further on that there are commandments that depend on the face, and some on the eyes and ears; and it says that "the LORD" is found in every single limb - He is found in the four colors of hair, and the four colors of the eye, and the four sections of the ear, and the four colors of the face, and in voice and speech and reading and utterance, and in the doing of the hands, and in every single limb of the body, "the LORD" is appointed over each and every commandment within it: a commandment [mitzvah], by the At-Bash cipher, [transforms into] Mem-Tzadi Yud-Heh Peh-Tzadi Vav-Heh - so "mitzvah" [becomes] "the LORD, Mitzpatz" - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:6: Now, from this a person will see how great a blemish he causes by blemishing one of his limbs - for since all the limbs are stamped with His Name, blessed be He, he is found to blemish the Name; and if he fulfills a commandment with that limb, happy is he, for he crowns "the LORD" over it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:7: Further, it is said in the Tikkunim (132a): "happy is he who causes Him to rest in each and every one of his limbs, making a place for Him to rest there and crowning Him in each and every limb, so that no limb is empty of Him - for if a single one is lacking such that the Holy One, blessed be He, does not rest upon it, because of that limb he must return to the world through transmigration [gilgul], until he is completed in his limbs, that they should all be complete in the image of the Holy One, blessed be He - for if one is lacking, he is not in the image of the Holy One, blessed be He. A crooked mouth - the Holy One, blessed be He, does not rest in it, for it is a defect; how much more so if its speech is crooked - of it is said (Ecclesiastes 1:15), 'that which is crooked cannot be made straight'" - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:8: Related to this blemish, it is further explained in the Tikkunim (111a), in these words: "certainly, whoever sins in his body - where the deed is - and in his soul - where the thought is - it is as though he sinned against the One in whose image he was created, as it is said (Genesis 1:27), 'and God created man in His image'" - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:9: Further, concerning the blemish inflicted upon the human body itself, Rashbi explains (Acharei 76a), on the verse (Job 16:8), "and my leanness rises up against me, testifying to my face" - in these words: "come and see: one who transgresses the words of the Torah - the Torah ascends and descends and makes marks upon that person's face, so that the upper and lower beings gaze upon him, and they all cast curses upon his head. And we have learned that all those 'eyes of the LORD' that go about and range through the world to know the ways of mankind, all lift their eyes and gaze upon that person's face and see them, and they all open [their mouths] against him, 'woe, woe!' - woe to him in this world, woe to him in the World to Come! Depart from around so-and-so, for there is a testimony on his face and an impure spirit rests upon him! And all those days that the mark remains on his face as a testimony, if he fathers a child, he draws down upon it a spirit from the impure side; and these are the stubborn-faced wicked of the generation, whom their Master allows to be destroyed in the World to Come.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:10: And we have learned: this righteous, worthy one who occupies himself with Torah day and night - the Holy One, blessed be He, draws over him a single thread of kindness, and it is marked on his face, and from that mark the upper and lower beings are in awe. Likewise, one who transgresses the words of the Torah draws upon himself an impure spirit, and it is marked on his face, and from him the upper and lower beings flee" - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:11: Above this it is explained that if one has sinned, he should weep and let the tears pass over his face until the mark passes away; and I have heard that it is also good to pass the tears over one's forehead, for iniquities are written on the forehead, in the manner of (Ezekiel 9:4), "and set a mark upon the foreheads of the men," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:12: Of this kind are the iniquities written on the hand, as it is written (Job 37:7), "He seals up the hand of every man." And so it is explained in the Tikkunim (142b), in these words: "and there are sins of which it is said, 'He seals up the hand of every man,' and they show them the sealing of their hands" - to this point. And this is also explained in Parashat Lech Lecha (78b), and we shall cite its words below, in chapter twelve.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:13: The second blemish is a blemish in the soul, that according to the sin committed, so it descends, until it is brought down to his feet. This is explained in the Tikkunim and in Ra'aya Meheimna. In the Tikkunim (132b): "come and see: there are people who speak with a movement of their eyes, others with a movement of their hands, others with a movement of their head, others with a movement of their body, and others with a movement of their feet - this is because wherever the soul is [located within him], it makes extra movement in that place." Rabbi Elazar said to him: father, is the soul not in a known place, in the heart, spreading forth to all the limbs of the body? He said to him: my son, is it not written of her (Ruth 3:7), "and she uncovered his feet and lay down"? According to a person's deeds, so she goes forth from her place and descends outside her place - similar to the Shechinah, of whom it is said (Isaiah 50:1), "and for your transgressions your mother was sent away." And complete repentance is when one returns her to her place as she was before - for at the time the soul is in the heart, she is called "Matrona" [Queen]; when she goes forth from the heart, she is not called "Matrona." According to a person's sins, so she descends from level to level and from limb to limb until she descends to his feet, and according to his merits, so she ascends until she ascends to her place; and therefore, wherever she descends, she makes extra movement in that limb more than in the others" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:14: Our Sages, of blessed memory, said (50a): and the soul in its final exile - of it is said, "and she uncovered his feet and lay down" - she lay down in the dust. Woe to the person whose soul has descended beneath his feet, for at that time it is said of her (Amos 5:2), "she has fallen, she shall no more rise," and there is no ascent or elevation for her except by the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He," and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:15: There is a third aspect of blemish: that according to the blemish a person causes in his soul, so he causes a blemish in the Shechinah, until she descends to the lowest level and "uncovers his feet." This is explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (Mishpatim 117b), in these words: "from the side of the wicked, even the good is lost to him [reading a difficult phrase] - the Shechinah - 'and she uncovered his feet and lay down' - this is (Proverbs 30:23), 'and a maidservant when she supplants her mistress' - the maidservant being the female evil inclination." And it explains afterward the matter of the blemish, saying: "but the Shechinah, of the Tree of Life, of her it is said (Psalms 5:5), 'evil shall not sojourn with You' - but if the maidservant rules, it is upon the Throne and below it."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:16: In these words: "but because it is said (ibid. 103:19), 'and His kingdom rules over all,' whoever blemishes her place is accounted as though he brought disgrace upon the Matrona - for the disgrace of the Matrona is one who demeans her place, and this is the disgrace of the King's Matrona; how much more so one who removes her from her place and puts a maidservant in her place! For in every place where he blemishes, the Matrona does not rest there, but rather the maidservant, who is blemished, rests in the blemished place. And a person's blemish from his sins blemishes all his limbs, until the Matrona finds no place to rest there; and there is no remedy until he restores to her all her limbs" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:17: And so it is also explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (Ki Teitzei 277b), in these words: "and this Malchut of Atzilut has, corresponding to it, the Malchut of Beriah, which is the sovereignty for the angels of Beriah, and she is the maiden of the Matrona, her attendant, and is the image of her mistress, comprising the ten [sefirot]. This one, through Israel's sins, can be profaned among the nations of the world; but the Malchut of Atzilut, of the Holy One, blessed be He, of her it is said (Isaiah 42:8), 'I am the LORD, that is My Name, and My glory I will not give to another, nor My praise to graven images' - it is not given to one who desecrates Sabbaths and festivals, but only to one who is a child of the King and keeps the Torah in fear and love of his Master, not for the sake of receiving a reward, but as a son who is obligated to carry out his father's commands, of whom it is said (Exodus 20:12), 'honor your father and your mother' - 'your father,' this is the Holy One, blessed be He; 'your mother,' this is the Shechinah. And with all this, whoever desecrates the maiden of the King is accounted as though he desecrated his own Matrona" - to this point. And this introduction is further explained in Parashat Pinchas (see 226a) - see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:18: Here it is explicitly explained, in this passage, the same likeness of the Shechinah as was said in the Tikkunim regarding the soul; and the reason is that the soul is literally a portion of the Shechinah, as it says (Deuteronomy 32:9), "for the LORD's portion is His people" - and the souls of Israel are from the secret of the [divine] union - "you are children to the LORD your God" (ibid. 14:1). And there is a union between the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah to bring forth a soul on the Sabbath day, and there is a union between them to bring forth a soul on weekdays - these being "nefesh" from the Throne, "ruach" from Chayah, "neshamah" from Ophan. And concerning the soul of the weekdays is the blemish mentioned in the passage, "he removes her from her place," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:19: Nevertheless, sometimes a blemish is found even in one who has a soul of Atzilut, as it is written in the Tikkunim (99b) concerning the sin of the first man: "in the place from which his soul was taken, there he sinned." And the reason is that according to what the souls do, which are the branches below, so they arouse an effect in the roots. And even though sin does not [normally] come through one who has a soul of Atzilut, nevertheless the withdrawal of the soul from him is what is called a blemish. And so it is explained in the Tikkunim (124a): "a person commits sins; according to that person, so his sin rises to the place from which his soul was hewn, and that sin does not move from there until payment is exacted from that person. And if a person's soul is of the path of Atzilut, if he sins, his sin reaches up to the sefirot, and the punishment is great, according to his level."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:20: Rabbi Elazar said: father, is sin then dependent on the person whose soul is from that place - does he really have [such power]? But it is written (Proverbs 12:21), "no harm shall befall the righteous"! He said to him: yes - this is [the meaning of] (Isaiah 59:2), "but your iniquities have separated between you and your God" - separated whom? Rather, that this soul of Atzilut is removed from him and separated from him; and the secret of the matter is (Genesis 1:9), "and God said, let the waters under the heaven be gathered together," and so on - his soul was removed from him and a dry body remained. What "body" is meant here? This is the soul of the Throne of Glory that remained dry, because the soul of the path of Atzilut was removed from him - for this soul [of the Throne] is a body for the supernal soul; and if it wishes to return to that soul, it has no permission to return to it until that sin is removed from it - and the secret of the matter is (Malachi 3:7), "return to Me, and I will return to you'" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:21: This, then, is an introduction to all the blemishes to be explained concerning the removal of the Mother from over the children, and so on - all of this follows this pattern; and one may distinguish between an individual and the multitude. There is a hint of proof for this in the Zohar (Vayikra 15b), which says that when the sins of the world increase, the Ancient Holy One conceals Himself, and there is no face-to-face gazing," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:22: Further, concerning the blemish of the Shechinah, it is explained in the Tikkunim (58b), in these words: "and when the middle pillar [Tiferet] distances itself from her, this is judgment, and of it is written (Psalms 75:8), 'for God is judge; He puts down one and lifts up another' - 'He puts down one' - whoever causes the Shechinah to be lowered from her place; 'and lifts up another' - whoever causes her to be raised to her place - for Israel's sins lower her down, and their merits raise her to her place; happy is he who performs merits to raise her to her place" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:23: Further, the blemish a person causes in the Shechinah and in the other levels below is explained by what is explained in the Tikkunim (65a): it says there that in the Shechinah are engraved souls, angels, and the holy Chayot, and engraved in her is what is said (Ezekiel 1:10), "and the likeness of their faces was the face of a man." Rabbi Shimon rose and said: Sabba, Sabba, is not the Shechinah the very unity of the Holy One, blessed be He - how can images of the lower beings be engraved in her, which are not her true reality? He said to him: [it is like] a king who sits in his palace, and many people come to see him - some gaze at his garments, some at his body, and some gaze at his deeds; and certainly through his deeds it becomes known who the king is, for garments change in many ways - the garments he wears in the morning he does not wear in the evening, and the garments he wears one day he does not wear the next day, and so on every day, month, year, Sabbath, and festival, the garments change.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:24: In this manner, the Shechinah has many garments, from which the Holy One, blessed be He, created thrones, angels, Chayot, seraphim, heaven and earth, and all that He created with them; and all the creatures He created from these garments of hers are all marked and engraved in her garments, so that all creatures may gaze upon her and have compassion upon them - and the secret of the matter is (Genesis 9:16), "and I will look upon it, to remember the everlasting covenant" - "and I will look upon it" - upon these garments that shine in all creatures, for Israel illuminates them through good deeds, and because of them the Holy One, blessed be He, loves them; and if they do evil deeds, she clothes herself in other, black garments, in which are marked all those masters of judgment, called "Lilith," to judge the world through them - and at that time she says (Song of Songs 1:6), "do not look at me, for I am dark," and so on. And therefore, from the side of these garments, supernal [images] are engraved in her," and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:25: We find, then, that all existing things are portrayed in these garments, and they are the roots within her of the reality of all the lower worlds; and when the roots within her shine through the commandments that Israel repairs below, there is mercy and good in the world; but when Israel does not repair its deeds, all her garments nurse from the side of judgment and darkness, and then she says, "do not look at me, for I am dark."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:26: With this we may understand what is said in the Tikkunim, printed in Parashat Bereshit (Zohar 23b): "whoever sins against the Shechinah is as though he stripped the Shechinah of her garments, and this is the punishment of Adam; and whoever fulfills a commandment of the Torah is as though he clothed the Shechinah in her garments" - to this point. The intent is that through sin one strips off her beautiful, shining garments and clothes her in garments of blackness, as explained in this passage.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:27: And it further says there (the Additions, 252b) that the Shechinah is the pupil of the eye [bat ayin], dark, with light shining within her from inside; and concerning this King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 27:1), "the LORD is my light" - the light of the Yud, which is the pupil of the eye. And it says: she has two colors, light within and darkness without, so that she may rule over all the husks [kelipot] through them - this is (ibid. 103:19), "and His kingdom rules over all" - in the garment of light she rules over all of whom it is said (Exodus 10:23), "and all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings," and in the garment of blackness she rules over all the wicked, of whom it is said (I Samuel 2:9), "and the wicked shall be silenced in darkness" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:28: From the root of the soul in which a person is rooted, he repairs or blemishes, as it is said, that souls are engraved within her; and therefore, by blemishing below, he darkens the root of his soul that is rooted in the Shechinah, and then, through his sin, good is withheld from him, for she has no "face" [standing] to request flow on his behalf.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:29: In this manner we may understand that the blemish a person causes, wherever he blemishes, is through the root of the soul that is rooted in all places - for the soul, in every place it passes through, leaves its form imprinted there. My teacher, peace be upon him, explained that it is through the root of the soul imprinted there that a person arouses "female waters" [mayin nukvin] within the Shechinah, by saying (Psalms 25:1), "to You, O LORD, I lift up my soul," as is explained in the Zohar (Vayakhel 202b; Bamidbar 120b); and if his soul is blemished, it certainly will not be included in the [divine] union and will not arouse anything, for since the branch is blemished, the root too is blemished.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:30: In this manner Rashbi explains (Terumah 129a) that Yehoyada'am is appointed over the images of the righteous, and he says there of one who brings the wicked back in repentance, that he arouses his soul above in union by saying, "to You, O LORD, I lift up my soul"; and Yehoyada'am carries his image upward, and they bless it with many blessings. In these words: "at that moment a certain appointed one is summoned, who is the treasurer over the images of the righteous, through the secret of the service of the letters, called by the secret name Yehoyada'am, in the crown of service of the Holy Name; and the Holy One, blessed be He, gives a sign, and that appointed one brings the image of that person who turns the souls of the wicked [to repentance], and it stands before the King and the Matrona - and I call heaven and earth to witness concerning him that at that moment that image is handed over to him, for there is no righteous person in this world whose image is not engraved above, under the hand of that appointed one, and seventy keys of all his Master's treasuries are placed in his hand; then the King blesses that image with all the blessings with which He blessed Abraham, for he has turned the souls of the wicked [to repentance]," and so on - to this point. And they elaborate further there on the virtue of one who turns the wicked to repentance, which is not our present concern.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:31: Further, it is explained in Parashat Vayeshev (Zohar 191a) that all forms are portrayed in the Shechinah; and it says there that when a person is complete in his image - meaning in the countenance of the soul, called "Adam," that he has not sinned - all creatures fear him, as it is written (Genesis 9:2), "and the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth," and so on. And it says: this applies when the soul is within him - meaning that he has not blemished his body such that the soul withdraws from him; but once there is a blemish in the body, the soul withdraws from him and he becomes like a beast, as it says (Psalms 49:13), "and man in his glory does not abide; he is like the beasts that perish" - and man's "glory" [yekar] is his soul, and whoever sins and causes the soul not to lodge within him is likened to the beasts.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:32: And he raised a difficulty: but of Daniel it is written (Daniel 6:23), "my God sent His angel and shut the lions' mouths, and they have not hurt me" - implying that it was the angel who shut them, not his own image. And he resolved it, that the angel itself is his image - meaning the image engraved in the Shechinah, called an angel - in these words: "he said to him: because of this he was not harmed, for that image of a righteous, worthy person is itself literally an angel that shuts their mouths and binds them, to guard him so that they should not harm him; and therefore, 'my God sent His angel' - the one in whom all the images of the world are engraved, and he strengthened his image within him, and they were unable to overpower me, and shut their mouths - and therefore 'He sent His angel' certainly. And this angel, in whom all images are engraved, of whom it is written (Psalms 110:6), 'He shall judge among the nations, filling [them] with corpses [or: bodies]' - he does not change before him from all the images of the world. Therefore a person must guard his ways and paths, so as not to sin before his Master, and so that he may endure in the image of Adam" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:33: Now that we know that all the images of the righteous are there [in the Shechinah], undoubtedly, if the image below is blemished, the image above will not be seen before the whole heavenly retinue, for "any who has a defect shall not draw near." And when a person considers this, he will feel shame and disgrace over his sins, for every single sin is a plague and a defect in his soul, and his image above becomes distanced from holiness - as Scripture says of the leper (Leviticus 13:45-46), "and the leper in whom the plague is, his garments shall be torn... and he shall cover his upper lip, and shall cry, unclean, unclean," and it says, "he shall dwell alone, outside the camp shall his dwelling be." The blemish in the soul, and its distancing from supernal holiness, is what causes the body below likewise to be distanced from the camp of Israel; and if a person repents to purify his defects by accepting suffering upon himself, he thereby purifies himself of his leprosy - but if not, that leprosy remains fixed in his soul, and in this world and the World to Come he is distanced from the whole heavenly retinue until he is purified. Therefore our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Yoma 22b) that King David, peace be upon him, was afflicted with leprosy for six months - for it is better that the blemish rise up in the body in this world than that the defect and leprosy remain in the soul, to be punished in Gehinnom.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:34: Further, this introduction is explained in the Tikkunim (65b) - that all souls are rooted there, and likewise regarding "ruach" and "neshamah" - in these words: "'set me as a seal' - this is the soul, whose mark is engraved above, as they established regarding Jacob, that Jacob's image is engraved on the Throne of Glory; for all souls that are hewn from there, their engraving is engraved above, and their mark is below - that supernal engraving is the 'seal,' and the lower mark is the 'mark of the seal.' And as soon as the mark of the soul's engraving is above, and its mark is below, it is said of it (Genesis 28:12), 'and behold, the angels of God ascending and descending upon it' - they ascend above and gaze upon the image of the soul that shines in that engraving, and they tremble because of it; they descend below and gaze upon the mark of that image below, and see that it has not changed from the image above, and they are in awe of it" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:35: Behold, when the lower image is in its proper state, without blemish, the angels fear it, because its image has not changed from the supernal image portrayed on the Throne. And it may be that of this it is said (Genesis 9:2), "and the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth and upon every bird of the sky" - "the beast of the earth" being the angels of the Shechinah, and "the bird of the sky" being the angels of the Holy One, blessed be He, in the manner explained in the Tikkunim (2b): "for a bird of the sky shall carry the voice" (Ecclesiastes 10:20) - this being Metatron.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:36: And in the Zohar (Noach 71a) it is explained "the beast of the earth," and so on, in its plain sense - saying that when the form of man is without sin, all creatures fear him, and if not, Heaven forfend, they all rule over him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:37: And in the Pekudin of Rabbi Shimon (Zohar, Naso 123b), this verse is explained in another manner, in these words: "and because everything was created in this image - for of all Israel, who are righteous, it is said, 'and the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth and upon every bird of the sky,' and so on - and this speaks of people who are likened to wild beasts, to cattle, to birds, and to the fish of the sea; for there is a person whose fortune [mazal] is an ox, and one whose fortune is a lion, and one whose fortune is an eagle, and one whose fortune is a man [adam] - and why do all these fear this image, from which they were created? Rather, because the Name 'the LORD' rests upon it, and the secret of the matter is (Deuteronomy 28:10), 'and all the peoples of the earth shall see,' and so on; and whoever blemishes his deeds, his image is blemished, and the Name 'the LORD' does not rest in a blemished place" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:38: And there, above this matter, it says that according to a person's deeds, so he merits the image of holiness or its opposite - in these words: "just as there is a good image over the righteous one, guiding him in all good deeds to merit him for the World to Come, so there is an evil image over the head of the wicked, to guide them in evil deeds, that they may inherit Gehinnom; and therefore there is 'hevel' [vanity/breath] and there is 'hevel' - there is a good 'hevel,' of which it is said (Deuteronomy 8:3), 'for by everything that proceeds from the mouth of the LORD does man live,' and there is an evil 'hevel,' of which it is said (Ecclesiastes 1:14), 'this too is vanity and a vexation of spirit.'"
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:39: Come and see: from a person's deeds, the countenance that rests upon him becomes known, and in the features of his face - this is (Isaiah 3:9), "the look of their faces testifies against them." From the image, the countenance of the "Chayah" that rests upon him becomes known - whether it is a lion, an ox, an eagle, or a man - from the Chariot of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, or from the Chariot of the angel, the Prince of the Countenance, or from the evil Chariot of Samael, or from the Chariot of the four elements of the world, in which there is neither good inclination nor evil inclination, but [only what is] like the animals of the world. And therefore there are many kinds of "hevel" among people, each according to its kind, and the secret of the matter is (Genesis 1:24), "let the earth bring forth the living creature after its kind"; and therefore, with the measure a person measures, he is measured" - to this point. And what he said, "there is a good 'hevel,' of which it is said, 'for by everything that proceeds from the mouth of the LORD,'" refers to the Shechinah, as is also explained there at the beginning of the passage - see there.
